notes:
This is a minor release: detection coverage expands, and existing settings, exports, and workflows are unchanged.

ENHANCEMENTS
• Unlabeled street addresses are marked when a house number and a street suffix appear together, so an address no longer needs an Address: label.
• Values split across two aligned lines are rejoined. A wrapped SSN in a table is still found.
• Common Unix paths such as /etc, /usr, /var, /opt, /srv, /tmp, and /root are detected. A path segment inside a URL stays with the URL rule.
• Names written as a pair, such as John/Jane Doe, are read as two name tokens for PII inference.

FIXES
• Comma-delimited rows keep the box on the matched field. An email in a CSV export no longer redacts the whole row.
• Markdown emphasis after a credential label no longer turns `**` into the secret. The password value is marked.
• Credential values on the next aligned line are marked, including access codes, gate codes, door codes, security codes, passcodes, and PINs.
• Property, billing, shipping, and similar addresses keep the full value through the city. A following label line is not swallowed.
• Overlapping address suggestions keep the full field box and drop contained fragments.
• Ticket IDs followed by a lowercase word after OCR are matched. Uppercase or digit continuations are still rejected.
• Code-shaped names and bare number pairs such as Gate 3 are no longer treated as names or addresses.
• CSV header cells are no longer treated as name fields.

The Windows installer remains unsigned; Windows may show an unknown-publisher warning. Linux and macOS builds are produced in CI without running the test suite on those platforms.
